small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_PW to 32 or 64 and reduce BLOCK_OC to 16; the inner outer-product is OC×PW, and wider PW gives better coalesced x loads since iw is contiguous. Sweep (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_PW) ∈ {(16,64),(32,32),(64,16)} with num_warps ∈ {4,8}.
- The current kernel recomputes the conv POOL*POOL=16 times per output. Cache conv results: compute conv on a (POOL+KH-1)×(POOL*BLOCK_PW+KW-1) input tile once, then reduce-max over the POOL×POOL window. This eliminates the 16× redundant MAC work.
- Hoist the weight load: load w[oc, ic, kh, kw] once per (ic,kh,kw) into a [BLOCK_OC] register and reuse across all POOL×POOL positions; currently weights are reloaded inside the pool loop.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM im2col conv where one program produces a full (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_OH_tile × BLOCK_OW_tile) conv output tile, then applies tanh/scale/bias and a POOL×POOL max-reduction in the epilogue. Use BLOCK_OH=BLOCK_OW=POOL (=4) so each program emits one pooled output per OC; this avoids the 16× recomputation in the current scheme.
- K-dim reduction loop should iterate over IC*KH*KW (=72) as the GEMM-K with tl.dot on [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K] × [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SPATIAL] tiles. With IC=8, KH=KW=3, OC=64, this fits a single tl.dot per program. Use BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SPATIAL=16 (4×4 pooled-window), num_warps=4.
- Consider a channels-last (NHWC) input layout transposed once in forward so the GEMM-K (IC) dimension is contiguous; this dramatically improves load coalescence vs. the current NCHW gather. Persist across PH·PW tiles per (N, OC-tile) program if launch overhead matters.
